title: Team roles guide
course: CIS 110 LN182 · Introduction to Computers · Fall 2026, second 8-week session

intro.eyebrow: Capstone project · game version · team roles
paragraphs: Each member of your team takes a role, and each role owns one part of the project. You declare your roles at checkpoint 2, on {long:C2}.
Owning a part means you make sure it gets done. Everyone still writes, comments, and requests changes.
intro.note: Roles are recorded in the **Team** sheet. Your role, version history, and comments show what you contributed.

edition.print_note: This is the printable version of the team roles guide. The web version is at `{site}`.

next.label: Next checkpoint
next.finished_text: Final submissions were due on {long:C7}. Watch Blackboard for your grade and feedback.

C1.summary: Join a team in Blackboard and introduce yourself in your team discussion.
C1.detail: Join a team in Blackboard. Then post a short introduction in your team discussion: when you can work, and what games you like. Use the team discussion to talk until your shared folder is ready.
todo: Join a team of {team_min} to {team_max} in Blackboard
Post an introduction in your team discussion
Reply to each teammate's introduction

C2.summary: Choose your game idea, give each person a role, and create your shared folder.
C2.detail: Each member pitches one game idea in the team discussion, and your team picks one. The Coordinator then creates the shared folder and shares it with everyone, including me. Each member declares a role by adding a row to the **Team** sheet. The Changes lead adds the first rows to the **Changes** sheet, and your team writes a short team charter.
todo: Pitch one game idea each in your team discussion
Choose one idea and a Coordinator as a team
Create the shared folder and add the three templates
Share the folder with every teammate and me as **Can edit**
Declare your role: add your row to the **Team** sheet
Changes lead: log your idea and roles in the **Changes** sheet

C3.summary: Have a draft of the design document in your folder.
C3.detail: Every heading in the design document has text. Each member leaves at least one comment on a section that someone else wrote.
todo: Write something under every heading in `GameDesign.docx`
Comment on one section a teammate wrote
Log this checkpoint's changes in the **Changes** sheet

C4.summary: Have a draft of the game data workbook in your folder.
C4.detail: The workbook has at least {min_rows} complete rows of game data, and every number in the design document appears in it.
todo: Fill at least {min_rows} complete rows in `GameData.xlsx`
Move every number from the design document into the workbook
Comment on one sheet a teammate filled
Log this checkpoint's changes in the **Changes** sheet

C5.summary: Have a draft of the presentation and its recording in your folder, so everything is in.
C5.detail: Every slide in the presentation has a draft, and one member has recorded a video presenting it, saved as `GamePitch.mp4`. After this deadline, I download your folder and build a playable prototype of your game over Thanksgiving break.
todo: Draft every slide in `GamePitch.pptx`
Draw a mock-up of one screen with shapes
Record one member presenting the slides, and save `GamePitch.mp4` in the folder
Comment on one slide a teammate made
Log this checkpoint's changes in the **Changes** sheet
C5.line: PowerPoint design summary and presentation recording in shared folder

C6.summary: Play your prototype and add your change requests.
C6.detail: From {links_by}, play the prototype I send you and add what should change to the **Changes** sheet. Each member adds at least one request by this date. You can keep adding requests until {long:C7}.
todo: Play your team's prototype
Add at least one change request each to the **Changes** sheet, with **Kind** set to **Request**
Read my replies and comments in your files

C7.summary: Submit your final files, the folder link, and each member's contribution.
C7.detail: Submit the folder link in Blackboard with one sentence about what each member contributed. Then complete the private peer rating survey in Blackboard. After this deadline, I plan to make a final pass on your game using your change requests.
todo: Make your final edits to all three files
Check that the **Changes** sheet is complete
Submit the folder link in Blackboard with each member's contribution
Complete the private peer rating survey

stats.label: Office files in one shared folder

status.break: No checkpoints. I build your games over the break.

sections.heading: What each role does
lede: Each card says what the role owns and what it does at each checkpoint.

items.title: Coordinator
items.text: Keeps the team on schedule and is the team's contact with me.
bullets: At checkpoint 2, creates the shared folder, adds the three templates, and shares it with each teammate and me as **Can edit**
Before each checkpoint, checks the to-do list on the assignment page and reminds the team in the team discussion
Keeps one copy of each file, with the template's file name, inside the shared folder
If a teammate goes quiet, follows the team charter, then sends me a Blackboard message
At checkpoint 7, submits the folder link with one sentence about what each member contributed

items.title: Design writer
items.text: Leads the design document and keeps it in the team's own words.
bullets: At checkpoint 3, makes sure every heading has text
Asks teammates in comments to write the parts they know best
Keeps rules and controls exact: a number, not a word like "fast"
Checks with the Data lead that every number in the document matches the workbook
Writes section 10 from what each member says about their AI use, one line per use

items.title: Data lead
items.text: Turns every number and list in the design into rows in the workbook.
bullets: At checkpoint 4, fills at least {min_rows} complete rows under the template's headers
Moves every number and list from the design document into the workbook
Writes a worked example and the expected result for each rule in the **Rules** sheet
Keeps the **Words** sheet: each term, what it means, and any word not to use for it
Keeps the sheet names and headers as they are, because I use them to find each part

items.title: Presenter
items.text: Builds the slides and records the presentation, or asks another member to record it.
bullets: At checkpoint 2, collects one pitch slide from each member
At checkpoint 5, builds the {slides_min} to {slides_max} slides, with the screen mock-up drawn with shapes
Keeps the slides in the team's own words, with more pictures and fewer words than the document
Records the {recording_min} to {recording_max} minute presentation and saves it as `GamePitch.mp4` in the folder

items.title: Art and sound lead
items.text: Finds or makes the images and sounds, and makes sure your team may use each one.
bullets: Finds or makes every image and sound the game uses
Lists each one in the **Assets** sheet: file name, who made it, license, and link
Writes section 8 of the design document, on the look, sound, and mood, with the Design writer
Leaves out any file without a license that allows reuse

items.title: Changes lead
items.text: Keeps the **Changes** sheet, your team's record of what changed and why.
bullets: At checkpoint 2, adds the first rows: the idea your team chose and who holds each role
Before each later checkpoint, checks that every change a teammate needs to know about has a row
Asks teammates to add rows for their own changes, and adds rows for changes nobody logged
After the prototype, makes sure each member adds at least one change request
Before checkpoint 7, reads the sheet top to bottom so the final pass has a clear list

sections.heading: Declare your roles
lede: Your roles are part of checkpoint 2, due {long:C2}. Do these steps in order.

items.title: Read the roles
items.text: Read this guide together and talk about it in your team discussion.

items.title: Choose
items.text: Agree who takes each role. In a smaller team, some people take two.

items.title: Create the folder
items.text: The Coordinator creates the shared folder and adds the three templates.

items.title: Declare your role
items.text: Add a row to the **Team** sheet in `GameData.xlsx`: your name and your role.

items.title: Log it
items.text: Add the first rows to the **Changes** sheet: the idea you chose and who holds each role.

items.title: Write the charter
items.text: Under the **Team** sheet, write when you meet, how you reach each other, and what you do if someone goes quiet.

sections.heading: In a smaller team
lede: There are more roles than people on most teams. Pair roles that fit together.

items.title: Team of five
items.text: One person takes two roles. The Coordinator often keeps the **Changes** sheet too, since both keep track of the team.

items.title: Team of four
items.text: Two people take two roles. Try Coordinator with Changes lead, and Presenter with Art and sound lead.

items.title: Team of three
items.text: Each person takes two roles. Try Coordinator with Changes lead, Design writer with Presenter, and Data lead with Art and sound lead.

items.title: Switching roles
items.text: You can switch at any checkpoint. Update the **Team** sheet, and add a row to the **Changes** sheet.

items.title: Does my role change my grade?
items.text: Your role doesn't change the points. Your documented contribution counts: a member without one might receive a different grade from the rest of the team.

items.title: What if two people want the same role?
items.text: One person owns it, and the other helps. Record both in the **Team** sheet, and say who owns it.

items.title: Who records the presentation?
items.text: The Presenter, or another member if the Presenter would rather not. Your voice is required, and your face on camera is optional.

items.title: What if the person in a role goes quiet?
items.text: Follow your team charter. Then send me a Blackboard message before the next checkpoint.
